description:
FILED s473t6a (Opus, 2026-09-17) by #1501 ROUND 8 (t6a), CHECK 2 of
t/op/ref.t.  PRE-EXISTING.  1 blessed row, and the GLOB position of #1628's
wrong-kind-dereference family.

PROBED (scratch/s473t6a/probes/globderef.pl, `use strict qw(refs subs)`,
perl 5.40.3 vs PCL 2ac855aa):

    my $s = 'foo'; my $r = \$s;
    eval { my $g = *$r }      perl DIES "Not a GLOB reference"
                              PCL  LIVES

#1628 (s484a) made a reference whose REFERENT IS A SCALAR refuse the CONTAINER
dereferences -- `$$hrr{k}`, `$$arr[0]`, `@$arr` -- through the one resolver
`%p-scalar-referent-p`.  The GLOB sigil was not part of that pass: `*$ref`
takes the symbolic/glob path and produces something instead of perl's fatal.

The row is t/op/ref.t test 198, `ok (!eval { *$rpvbm }, 'PVBM ref is not a
GLOB ref')`.  ITS NAME IS MISLEADING and the round corrected the baseline for
it: `my $pvbm = PVBM;` is the plain STRING 'foo', so nothing in the assertion
is about a Boyer-Moore SV.  The three sibling rows (`PVBM is not a GLOB /
SCALAR / ARRAY ref`) are a DIFFERENT fact -- `*$s` / `$$s` / `@$s` on the
plain string under `use strict 'refs'` -- and now cite
`NS:use strict 'refs' is not enforced` (#1390).

FIX SHAPE: one arm at the glob-cast entry (`p-cast-*` / whatever
`*$expr` lowers to), asking `%p-scalar-referent-p` exactly as the container
casts do since #1628, and raising perl's "Not a GLOB reference".  PROBE THE
BREAKING CASE FIRST: a glob VALUE in that position is LEGAL (that is #1726,
s484c, and Carp depends on it), and `*$name` with a STRING is the SYMBOLIC
glob lookup, which must keep working under `no strict 'refs'` -- so the new
fatal is for a BOX whose referent is a plain scalar, nothing else.
subject: *$ref where the referent is a SCALAR must die "Not a GLOB reference"; PCL lives -- the GLOB position of #1628's wrong-kind-dereference family
